notes.title: Running Lati to the Party
notes.content:
Lati's mother left when she was 8.

Jake, Lati's brother was hit by a car. The ambulance arrived too late, leaving the medical staff no chance of saving him. This incident broke Lati’s family apart.
 She couldn’t handle losing her son and she couldn’t deal with the father who went into complete meltdown, drowning his sorrows in liquor. One day she just packed her bags and vanished.

When Lati was in high school, she was noticed by her gym trainer as a “gifted runner”. She knew that even if she screwed up her education she could fall back to a sports scholarship. But that was a backup plan, cause Lati aimed for more - she dreamed of making it as an artist.

Nearing the end of High School, and old friend called Hangman, who she had met at school approached Lati, nagging her for help in a store robbery - apparently it was going to be his rite of passage to become a "real gangster". He said that "she owes him" for all the times he's helped her out - so she couldn't refuse. They chose an inconspicuous shop run by an odd pair of clerks.

It ended in a bloody mess and dead clerks. 
As well as most of the crew. Hangman escaped, leaving Lati among the dead bodies.
In that moment of despair, an unlikely saviour emerged - Bob, a mysterious, moustached man on the wrong side of forty helped her to clean up that bloody mess and slip through the police patrol. Fully realizing she really had no home to go back to, she agreed to stick with Bob, at least for a while. That  turned into nearly a decade. Soon after, she met the other Cleaners.

notes.title: Cleaning Hacks Part 2
notes.content:
Here are a few more cleaning hacks to help blow the cobwebs and evidence away in Serial Cleaners.

1: Knock Knock - If you are precise enough, you can open a door in an enemy's face. This will knock them straight over giving you enough time to make a clean getaway.

2: Don’t Be a Drag - Dragging a body will cause extra mess.
This mess is extra mess you will have to clean up as it gets added to your vacuuming bar! But if you wrap up a body in a bag, it will leave no blood trail while being dragged.
It will also draw no attention to civilians when carried around public places.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38038000/d8c921588b969098f6285960df3dc83c9c547be5.jpg[/img]

3: Timing is Key - If you can time it right, you can lock a police officer inside a room, making your job that much easier... but you will need to have the correct key first.

4: Move without Sound – Pro-crime scene cleaners are never seen or heard.
While inside a crime scene, crouching allows you to move without making a sound. You can also hide behind low obstacles, so an enemy cannot see you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38038000/1870134c875bcd757f8b0c85203551afc4fc0aaa.jpg[/img]

5: Hide and Seek - If you are playing as Psycho, you can knocked-down enemies, pick them up, and then hide their unconscious bodies in various designated spots. This means that your cleaning job has just become a little more straightforward – so knock yourself out! …well, the enemies.

notes.title: Cleaning Hacks Part 1
notes.content:
[b]Here are some useful tricks and tips to help you clean up on Serial Cleaners.[/b]

[b]1: Need to Vent[/b] – Viper is the only character that can fit into small vents. She can't drag a body through a vent, but a big piece of evidence will fit through nicely.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38038000/ebf473b4a13727dc04d29caca8d94983b833365a.png[/img]

[b]2: Your Attention Please [/b]– utilise your surroundings! An open door will draw a police officer’s attention. Use that as a decoy, to draw them away from your location.

[b]3: Three is the Tragic Number[/b] - The police will not use lethal force straight away. But if they spot you three times or you attack them directly, that’s when they will draw their weapons.

[b]4: Escape Plan[/b] – It’s possible to outrun your enemies. Remember to use Lati’s speed and agility when you need it to outrun guards or police to make your escape. And when you do need to make a quick getaway, make sure it’s to “higher ground”.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38038000/43a90218d3cb56368928c0eaae1512c7fe7ec793.png[/img]

[b]5: Table Manners[/b] - If you are spotted by the police, run to the nearest hiding spot. There are many hiding places - a bed or a table. If you are being chased by the police, go to the nearest hiding place - the police officers will attempt to pull you out, but with a quickly timed jump out of hiding into the direction of the officer will knock them over so you can escape.
Remember, “Cleaner Sense” will tell you where the police are, but it will also tell you where your hiding spots are, so make sure you use it!

notes.title: What About Bob?
notes.content:
In the '70s Bob was a contractor for the mob. 

He made enough money to pay rent and support his mother. In the following years, Bob dabbled in gambling and ended up in a lot of debt.
He found himself involved in a lot of risky jobs for some unknown contractor, which later turned out to be the mother of the Echo Killer - a soon-to-be-famous copycat serial killer. 
Echo Killer was eventually caught by the police with Bob's help - but Bob was seriously injured during his capture. It took a while, but once Bob recovered, he packed his bags and took his mother and left town.

In the early '80s, Bob moved to the East Coast, with the goal of becoming a new man. Someone law-abiding. He was no longer 'The Cleaner'. 
His mother's health was declining, so he took a job as a janitor in one of the local offices. 
He was missing something - he preferred the thrill of his previous job to this mundane existence, but he was doing this to take care of his mother. 

After his mother passed away, Bob realised the life of a decent man just wasn't for him and through one of his contacts, Bob got back into work - this time for a drug lord. 
Bob spent the next few years drowning his sorrows before cutting ties with that part of his life - after one event in Miami where his paranoid boss wiped all of his own henchmen. He had asked his favourite wise-guy Bob, to clean up after him. 

In the early 90s, Bob moved to NYC to do what he does best - cleaning. With an apartment in the Meatpacking District and a deal with Crawford & Simms Funeral Home to have as an "office", he got recognized by mob boss Don Reina. It was soon after this, he met the rest of the Serial Cleaners.

notes.title: Check out the brand new stealth-focused gameplay trailer!
notes.content:
[h1]Hello dear followers of Serial Cleaners, I hope you're all doing very well![/h1]

As the development process of [b]Serial Cleaners[/b] continues, the internal builds are getting richer and richer with features, mechanics and systems. One of the goals we set ourselves while working on the design pillars of the game months ago, was to reach several different target groups of players, some very different from the other...

One of such target groups is a community of fans of stealth games. Stealth as a genre boasts many sub-genres and sets of distinctive features, influencing the perspective, difficulty level, pace and dynamics, level design etc. All in all, there are squad- and turn-based, very challenging and demanding extensive planning stealth games, and there are solo, fast and arcade'y stealth games. And all in between. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38038000/a927e827070c7b8f4a99da5bb7f837c206e52d9b.png[/img]

This versatility allows us to design [b]Serial Cleaners[/b] as a partly stealth game the way we like most. Stealth elements in our game are one of the most important, and we're putting lots of emphasis on providing a high-quality stealth experience!

Out latest gameplay trailer, prepared specifically for our friends at [b][url=https://www.gamespot.com/]Gamespot[/url][/b] focuses exactly on two out of four playable anti-heroes, who have to clean up some messy crime scenes: Bob and Psycho. The map is called [b]Cabin[/b] and is heavily inspired by the cult [b]Fargo[/b] movie.
